data.body_html:
Dolphin watching in Marbella is a bucket-list experience, and timing is everything. The best time of year for dolphin watching in Marbella in 2050 is June to September, when sea temperatures hit 22-26°C and sightings are almost guaranteed. But dolphins are present year-round, and with the right planning, you can spot them in spring or autumn too. This guide covers peak months, daily timing, and how to book your perfect charter from Puerto Banús.

Our fleet of 20+ boats includes everything from speedy 6.4m runabouts to luxurious 29m yachts, all departing from Puerto Banús. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and VAT — so you can focus on the dolphins.

Why June to September Is the Best Time for Dolphin Watching

Summer in Marbella brings stable weather, calm seas, and abundant marine life. From June to September, water temperatures are warm, and dolphins are most active near the coast. Sightings of bottlenose, striped, and common dolphins are frequent — with a success rate above 95%.

Average sea temperatures: June 22°C, July 24°C, August 26°C, September 24°C. Air temperatures range from 25°C to 35°C, making early morning trips comfortable. Book a 2-hour charter on our boat rental Marbella fleet for a quick adventure, or an 8-hour trip to explore further along the coast.

Best Time of Day for Dolphin Sightings

Early morning (08:00-10:00) is the prime window. The sea is calmest, giving you the best chance to spot dolphins breaking the surface. Afternoons often bring the Poniente wind, which creates chop and can make sightings harder.

Our Tier A boats — the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) — start at €749 for 2 hours, including skipper and refreshments. For larger groups, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) from €4,719 for 4 hours includes a free jet ski.

Can You See Dolphins in Spring and Autumn?

Yes. Spring (April-May) and autumn (October-November) offer good sightings, though less frequent than summer. Water temps range from 16°C to 22°C, and crowds are smaller. You'll enjoy a quieter experience with the same expert skippers.

Our boats operate year-round, so you can book any month. The Bandido (11.5m, 8 pax) and Pershing 46 (14m, 10 pax) are popular off-season choices. Check availability via WhatsApp for pricing on these models.

Winter Dolphin Watching in Marbella

Winter (December-February) sees fewer tourists, but dolphins are still present. Water temps drop to around 15°C, so dress warmly. Sightings are less predictable, but the calm winter seas can be excellent for spotting.

Our Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) and Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) are ideal for small groups. All charters include hot drinks and snacks. Book a 2-hour trip for a quick winter escape.

What to Expect on a Dolphin Watching Charter

Every charter includes a licensed skipper who knows the best spots — often near Cala del Faro, Cala Cortés, or off the coast of Estepona. You'll also get fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and 21% VAT.

Our larger boats, like the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) and Canados 86 (26m, 12 pax), offer spacious decks and shaded areas. For a more intimate experience, the Azimut 39 or Astondoa 40 are perfect.

How to Book Your Dolphin Watching Charter

Booking is simple. Choose your boat from our fleet, then contact us via WhatsApp for availability and pricing. For Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39), you can book directly at €749/2h or €2,299/8h. For Tier B boats like the Mangusta 80, the minimum is 4 hours at €4,719.

All charters depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella's iconic marina. We recommend booking at least 48 hours in advance, especially in summer. For the best time of year for dolphin watching in Marbella — June to September — early booking is essential.
